assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases are a clean, universal mechanism: a phase acquired from the geometry of parameter or gauge space, not from dynamics. The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry's 1984 phase underlie Hall quantisation, polarisation theory, topological band theory and molecular physics. Foundational work whose consequences everywhere are well understood, which is the kind of idea I trust.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov-Bohm (1959) and Berry (1984) are the two clear anchors; Aharonov-Berry two-person configuration is coherent. David Bohm is deceased and cannot be credited, and Pancharatnam's earlier phase and Simon's holonomy interpretation are historical complications I cannot independently verify here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed experimentally for decades (Tonomura electron holography, optical and NMR Berry-phase experiments, topological matter); very mature, arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as one discovery or two (Aharonov-Bohm versus Berry); Bohm's deceased status and Pancharatnam's priority may weaken a fair credit story; the exact experimental decisiveness of the original AB confirmations has been debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity, opened moire quantum matter. A simple model with a surprising universal consequence, tested directly by experiment and spawning a large field.
assessment.attribution: Theory-experiment pairing is natural: Bistritzer and MacDonald for the flat-band mechanism, Jarillo-Herrero for the experimental discovery. Cao and others on the experimental side and earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) raise priority questions I cannot resolve; MacDonald is also credited elsewhere on the longlist.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups across graphene and TMD moire systems within about eight years, though the superconducting mechanism remains unsettled; likely on the early side but very strong.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved; priority of earlier theory; limiting to three names omits first author of the 2018 experiments (Yuan Cao) and other experimentalists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (Z2 classification, quantum spin Hall effect) introduced a new organising principle for band insulators, with robust edge states and wide influence on condensed matter, photonics and mathematical physics. Clear, original theory with decisive experimental confirmation.
assessment.attribution: Kane-Mele for the Z2 theory; Molenkamp's group for HgTe quantum wells realising the quantum spin Hall effect (with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicting it). Fu, Kane, Mele and Moore-Balents on 3D topological insulators, and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, complicate a three-person split.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed (HgTe, Bi2Se3 family by ARPES), well over fifteen years old; mature. Applications remain limited but the concept is secure.
uncertainties: Competing credit with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents; Haldane's 2016 recognition partly overlaps in topological band-theory territory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture proposes a critical point governing rigidity of disordered matter, with isostaticity, anomalous vibrational modes and universal scaling. This is the sort of simple, general mechanism behind a messy phenomenon (foams, grains, glasses, suspensions) that I value, and it connects soft matter to statistical physics of disordered systems.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 proposal and the 2003 O'Hern et al. numerics are the core; this is a natural two-person credit. O'Hern, Silbert and Wyart contributed essential later steps, and the exact-solution approach in infinite dimensions (Parisi, Zamponi and colleagues) developed a separate mean-field picture.
assessment.maturity: Strong numerical and experimental support, with mean-field theory in infinite dimensions; still some debate on the true nature of jamming criticality in finite dimension and its relation to the glass transition.
uncertainties: Universality class and finite-dimensional critical exponents remain debated; practical or technological impact is diffuse; the relation to the glass transition is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Crackling noise and depinning: universal avalanche statistics, scaling and renormalisation-group treatment of driven disordered systems, from Barkhausen noise to earthquakes and plasticity. A beautiful application of critical-phenomena ideas to out-of-equilibrium disordered systems, analysed rigorously.
assessment.attribution: D. S. Fisher's functional RG for depinning is the theoretical core; Sethna and Dahmen's Barkhausen avalanche theory and experiments connect it to magnets. Narrow set of names fairly captures the primary line, but Middleton, Narayan, Le Doussal, Wiese, Alava and others also contributed to the field.
assessment.maturity: Predictions have been compared with Barkhausen and other experiments with reasonable success, but quantitative universality is partial and the theory is still being refined; mature in concept but less crisp than some competitors.
uncertainties: Mixed experimental agreement on exponents; broad attribution spread across the depinning community; relative importance of Fisher's RG versus the Sethna-Dahmen avalanche theory may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level, built on Katori's magic-wavelength lattice idea and Ye's demonstration of extreme precision and coherence, give a thousandfold improvement in time metrology with consequences for fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. Clear, specific and impactful.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed magic-wavelength trapping of Sr atoms; Ye's group (JILA) pushed accuracy and stability to record levels. Two-person configuration is natural, though Hall and Hansch already received the 2005 prize for frequency combs on which the clocks depend, and ion-clock work (Wineland, Rosenband) is a neighbouring line.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs agree at the 10^-18 level, but the redefinition of the SI second is still pending and the technology is still advancing; arguably slightly early.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition in frequency metrology; whether the committee wants to recognise a technology still evolving; contributions of other lattice-clock groups (Lemke, Ludlow, Bloom) not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters: the Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the superfluid-Mott insulator transition observed by Greiner et al. link statistical mechanics of strongly correlated systems to controllable experiments. Quantum gas microscopes have extended this. Conceptually attractive from a many-body viewpoint.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) for theory, Greiner (and Bloch) for the Mott-transition experiment, Bloch for subsequent development; Esslinger and Cirac are equally defensible, so any three-person split is contested and the list has five names.
assessment.maturity: Many groups confirm; cold-atom quantum simulation is mature, though it has not yet answered an open question beyond what classical methods can do. Bose-Einstein condensation was already recognised in 2001.
uncertainties: Five-person credit cannot fit in one prize; Greiner's and Esslinger's relative standing; overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with neutral-atom quantum computing candidates; the scientific payoff beyond benchmark models is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermittency and multifractal scaling in fully developed turbulence address a central unsolved problem in classical physics, close to my own field. Frisch's multifractal and Parisi-Frisch formulation and Sreenivasan's experimental scaling work are important, but there is still no first-principles derivation of anomalous exponents, so this is a deep problem not yet cleanly solved.
assessment.attribution: Frisch (with Parisi) for multifractal formalism and Sreenivasan for experimental and data analysis contributions; Kolmogorov, Parisi, Kraichnan and Anselmet-type measurements show attribution is spread, and Kolmogorov is deceased. The two-person configuration is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Experimental and numerical evidence support anomalous scaling, but the interpretation is not stable: no theory explains the exponents and the multifractal model is phenomenological. Recognition would be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Absence of a derived theory of anomalous exponents; whether multifractal phenomenology counts as a discovery; Parisi was recognised in 2021 for other work; I am a practitioner in a neighbouring field and may over- or under-weight it.
